title: hour-boundary-attribution-drift-causing-billing-imbalance
creator: Diego Alvarez
description:
Summary: Production customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private reported week-over-week invoice deltas that did not match their observed API traffic. Investigation showed a subtle hour-boundary attribution drift combined with batch coalescing that moved small token volumes across hourly ledger windows, creating systematic +/- rounding artifacts that accumulated into visible billing deltas for long-lived tenants. This ticket covers root-cause analysis, the immediate production mitigation, and the longer-term guardrails to prevent recurrence.

Symptoms observed: multiple customers (incidents reported by SRE and CS) saw invoice lines shifted by 1 hour or showing fractional token blocks aggregated into neighboring hours. Discrepancies surfaced most often after rolling upgrades or autoscaler events and were most visible for Dedicated and Private clusters with non-zero NTP offsets and aggressive batching. Hosted customers saw smaller but reproducible rounding shifts when proxy multiplexing and fallback routing bumped requests between worker pools.

Scope: Affects aggregator pipeline that consolidates per-request token usage into hourly ledgers before downstream rollup. Manifested in Hosted (low magnitude), Dedicated (medium), Private (highest magnitude when cluster clocks were slightly skewed).

Impact: High for a subset of customers with steady streaming workloads or very tight billing reconciliation processes. Several enterprise customers opened escalations; accounting teams requested backdated reconciliation exports.

Goal: ship a safe hotfix to stabilize ledger attribution for the immediate billing cycle, provide backfill tools for affected customers, and implement durable fixes: monotonic session tagging, boundary-truncation on batch emission, and a slack-tolerant hour-windowing algorithm.
comments: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after CS escalations from two enterprise customers (Acct 1092, Acct 2148). Initial triage by SRE: suspected time-window misattribution. Assigned to Priya for ownership.

2026-03-02: Reproduced locally by simulating a 350ms NTP offset and aggressive batch coalescing. Repro steps added to notes. Observed token counts moved into previous hour when batch flush occurred during boundary. Added test harness to integration suite (link in attachments).

2026-03-03: Emergency meeting with Infra and Runtime teams. Agreed immediate mitigation: enforce per-request monotonic sequence IDs at proxy ingress (to avoid interleaving across hour boundaries) and add a server-side guard to not attach a previous-hour timestamp when batch flush occurs within 5s of boundary. Canary patch prepared.

2026-03-04: Canary rollout to one Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 (pool-id: ded-eu-4). Observed no additional hour-shifted events during 48h canary. Metrics dashboard (links) show reduced cross-boundary emissions. CS notified and asked to pause outbound billing adjustments pending full rollout.

2026-03-06: Small regression discovered: private clusters with offline KMS and slow clock sync still emitted boundary-ambiguous batches. Added a hard truncation that assigns tokens to the flush-window owner based on ingress epoch instead of flush time. Patch ready in branch ENG-582413/boundary-fix.

2026-03-08: Hotfix merged and deployed to Hosted control plane and Dedicated staging; Private fix packaged for customer upgrade (owner: support-engineering). Draft customer communication and reconciliation export attached. Marked follow-up tasks for backfill tool and unit tests.

2026-03-10: PR review complete. Post-deploy validation shows hour-window drift reduced >98% in targeted tenants. Still seeing residual rounding at sub-token level due to legacy ledger rounding rules; opened follow-up ticket to adjust rounding policy and add audit logs.
investigation_findings: Root cause is a combination of (1) batch flush logic that stamped emission-time onto ledger entries instead of original ingress-time, and (2) per-cluster clock skew (NTP offsets up to ~400ms) that allowed batches crossing the hour boundary to be attributed to the wrong hour. Additionally, proxy-level connection handovers could replay requests to a different worker and reassign a new flush timestamp, amplifying the window drift. The ledger rollup pipeline assumed deterministic per-request anchoring which broke under these operational conditions.
mitigation_plan: Immediate: patched emission code to use ingress epoch as authoritative timestamp for ledger attribution; added a 5s slack rule at hour boundaries to prefer earlier window; enforced monotonic per-request sequence IDs at proxy ingress. Short term: ship hotfix to Hosted/Dedicated and build customer upgrade package for Private. Medium term: add unit/integration tests that simulate clock skew and boundary flush; implement audit logs for each ledger write; update rounding policy to keep per-token accounting idempotent. Long term: rework rollup to use append-only monotonic counters and window alignment based on ingress time, plus operator tooling to backfill affected windows.
next_steps: Finalize backfill tool to reconstruct affected hourly ledgers and produce reconciliation exports (owner: DataInfra)
Coordinate with Support to offer invoice adjustments or credit where appropriate (owner: CS)
Add regression tests to CI that inject NTP skew and simulate batch flush at boundaries (owner: Runtime)
Ship private-cluster upgrade package and verify KMS/downtime upgrade path (owner: PrivateOps)
Close monitoring gaps: add alert for >0.5% cross-hour token movement in a single tenant over 24h (owner: Observability)
Open follow-up ticket to change rounding to per-token integer ledger (ENG-582414)
Write post-incident writeup and share with affected customers (owner: SRE)
Schedule security review for audit log changes if required (owner: Security)
